SC: Indicate (e.g. in segment GIR) the secondary (sub-) level of a Customs tariff number.
DA: A unique number, consisting of a fixed 13-digits part. It allows the unique identification of a particular type of Returnable Asset.
DB: A unique number, consisting of a fixed 13-digits part and a mandatory Serial Number of up to 16 digits. The fixed part allows for the unique identification of a particular kind of Returnable Asset, the second part is assigned to distinguish individual assets within a given Returnable Asset type.
DC: A unique number that identify a consignment comprised of one or more logistic units that are intended to be transported together.
DD: A unique number that identify a shipment comprised of one or more logistic units that are intended to be delivered together.
IL: Sequential numerical assignment to identical invoiced goods which are subject to the same conditions of sale.
ZZZ: Object identification mutually agreed between interchanging parties.
VV: Unique serial number assigned by the manufacturer that distinguishes one vehicle from another.
VW: A number identifying a skid or pallet.
VZ: The identification of a transport unit according to ISO/IEC 15459 (ISO: International Organization for Standardization. IEC: International Electrotechnical Commission).
BA: The identity number of a question in a questionnaire.
BC: The check digit of the primary number.
BD: The number which identifies the telephone equipment fitted to the vehicle.
BE: Products manufactured in Batch not to be included in consignment.
BF: The number on the key that fits the door lock.
BG: The number of the fleet to which a vehicle is assigned.
BH: The number on the key that fits the ignition lock.
BI: The security code number of the radio.
BK: The unit number of the vehicle within the fleet allocated by the fleet operator.
BL: The registration number of the vehicle.
BM: A reference number identifying the accounting classification.
BN: Identification number of an item which distinguishes this specific item out of a number of identical items.
BP: A reference number identifying a special accounting classification.
BR: A code identifying a transportation account.
BS: A code identifying financial details for accounting.
BT: A code identifying the account manager.
BU: [1438] Unique number allocated by the buyer to identify an individual package.
BV: Identity number is a predecessor constraint.
BW: Identity number is a successor constraint.
BX: Unique number affixed by manufacturer to a batch of products produced under similar conditions.
BY: The identity number of a person.
BZ: The identity number of a health-care professional.
EE: Unique number affixed by manufacturer to an engine for identification purposes.
EF: A number identifying a coupon which is attached to the identified product.
EH: A unique number, up to 14-digits, assigned according to the numbering structure of the GS1 system, to identify a trade item.
EI: The International Mobile Station Equipment Identity (IMEI) is a unique number to identify mobile phones. It includes the origin, model and serial number of the device. The structure is specified in 3GPP TS 23.003.
EM: Manufacturer assigned reference to a photographic product indicating sensitivity.
WA: The identification of an indivisible transport unit according to ISO/IEC 15459 (ISO: International Organization for Standardization. IEC: International Electrotechnical Commission).
WB: The identification of a divisible transport unit according to ISO/IEC 15459 (ISO: International Organization for Standardization. IEC: International Electrotechnical Commission).
ML: The number on the marking or label.
CA: The identity number of a private institution.
CB: The identity number of a public institution.
CC: The identity number of a structure containing two or more objects linked in a hierarchy.
CD: The identity number of a subset of a structure containing two or more objects linked in a hierarchy.
CE: The identity number of a set of links.
CF: The identity number of an organisation chart.
CG: Identity number assigned to a healthcare provider by a non-government body.
CI: A unique identifier assigned to an insurer.
CJ: Identity number of a healthcare service provider issued by a hospital.
CK: Uniquely identifies the practice in which one or more healthcare providers conduct business.
CL: A unique identifier assigned to an agent.
CM: The identification number of the insurer's group.
CN: Unique number affixed by manufacturer to a chassis for identification purposes.
CQ: Control number assigned for internal use.
CU: Unique number, consisting of the GS1 Company Prefix and an Individual Asset Reference.
CV: A band attached to the leg of a live animal to uniquely identify the animal.
CW: A number registered by an authority to identify a particular commodity or goods.
CX: An identification tag affixed to a commodity or goods, e.g. livestock.
CY: A tattooed identification, e.g. on livestock.
CZ: An identification band attached to the wing of a bird.
PN: Manufacturer-assigned reference to a product part.
AA: A number that is used to identify goods from a freight forwarder/consolidator.
AB: The first element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AC: The second element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AD: The third element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AE: The fourth element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AF: The fifth element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AG: The sixth element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AH: The seventh element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AI: The eighth element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AJ: The ninth element in a series of elements that together define the structure of an object.
AK: The identity of a data set.
AL: [1420] Reference number to identify a kanban card.
AM: Level number in a hierarchy or other structure.
AN: A unique number identifying a particular assembly or other manufacturing process.
AO: A number to identify the position within a package according to agreed rules between partners.
AP: A name or number which identifies a product.
AS: A table of items e.g. figures and text represented in rows and columns.
AT: Number identifying a group of articles in a predescribed unit load for shipment/dispatch as agreed between partners.
AU: A coded or non coded list of values.
AV: A subset of a coded or non coded list of values.
AW: A single unique serial number which identifies shipping containers or shipping packages.
AX: A code to identify the number assigned to a given case.
AY: Identification number of a financial security.
AZ: The security code number of the compact disk player.
